executive_summary:
JD Sports Fashion Plc is a sterling global sports-fashion retailer. North America is now the largest region. The quantitative screen still prints buy: 11/22 models, composite 0.6912 versus a sector-relative 0.599, all five families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk). That label is not clean. Snapshot failed_models is empty despite 11 models not passing; fcf_definition_divergence, cyclical_exposure_overlay, cash_conversion_overlay and interim_quality_overlay stay false on a three-way FCF split, a sneaker-cycle retailer, and empty Yahoo quarterlies. Conviction_score is 1.0 while the same snapshot summary says “Conviction 64%”; the attached screen_run_manifest (30 August 2026) has conviction_score 0.4003 and weeks_at_signal 1. The snapshot signal is 12-week persistent / stable since 2 August 2026 and straddles the 20 August warning. Timing is neutral (RSI 38.8, price +1.0% versus the 200-day). trade_plan is null; the summary embeds limits £80.66 / £77.41 (stop £72.71, target £87.71) on an ~80p name. Those strings read as pounds, not pence. The snapshot already seeds an Accumulate / Medium-risk overlay and repeats that paragraph many times; this synthesis does not treat that seed as authority.

The assigned annual bodies are real, but they are not a live operating print. Companies House Annual Report & Accounts 2026 (52 weeks to 31 January 2026; filed 5 August 2026) are GBP: revenue £12,662m (+10.5%), LFL −2.1%, profit before tax and adjusting items £852m (−7.7%), statutory basic EPS 8.63p (−9.2%), company-defined free cash flow £462m, net leverage 1.4x, net cash excluding leases about £311m, £200m buyback completed and a further £200m programme for FY27, proposed dividend 1.20p. The FY26 extract is truncated before the financial statements. The only company-authored results RNS in the pack is FY25 (21 May 2025): revenue £11,458m, adjusted PBT £923m, statutory PBT £715m, operating cashflow net of lease repayments £1,245m, net cash before leases £52m, Genesis 20% NCI put/call capped at £1.5bn. There is no indexed interim and no indexed trading update.

Do not endorse the 12-week Buy. Company FCF of £462m covers Yahoo cash dividends of £52m and the £201m FY26 repurchase and does not require the screen’s 21.4% FCF yield; Yahoo FCF of £956m is OCF minus capex and ignores the FY26 KPI change; screen FCF of £830m is a third, unreconciled figure. Accumulate on filing-visible cash generation, a lease-ex net-cash residual near £311m, and cheap multiples; treat the headline Buy, the empty failed_models list, the pounds-versus-pence limit stack, and any book sized off the missing 20 August trading update as unsafe.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s five-family pass describes a single-digit earnings multiple and a 1.4% trailing yield on a sports-fashion name, not a confirmed through-cycle cash compounder. Passed models are Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score, Composite Value and Earnings Quality. Conflict check versus `screen_run_manifest.json` (not enumerated in the screen worker): the 11 non-passes are Graham Defensive (0.75), Graham Enterprising (0.60), Graham Net-Net (0.00), Schloss (0.00), Deep Value (0.50), Lynch PEG (0.20), Quality Value (0.60), Buffett Quality (0.25), Economic Moat (0.00), High Dividend Yield (0.107) and Financial Health (0.80). Snapshot failed_models remains []. P/E 9.0, P/B 1.3, yield 1.4%, ROE 13.7% and FCF yield 21.4% are screen prints. Data quality 20/20 does not repair an empty failed-model list, a suppressed TTM cash-flow field, or cyclical and FCF-definition flags that never fired.

For a value investor the hook is still cash and a shrinking share count — if, and only if, company-definition sterling free cash flow covers the cash dividend after leases and capex, and if North America plus footwear can stabilise after a news-only FY27 cut. FY26 company FCF of £462m covered Yahoo cash dividends of £52m at about 8.9x and covered dividend-plus-buybacks of about £253m at about 1.8x. Yahoo FCF of £956m would make that cover look trivial only because it never applies the company’s new free-cash definition. Screen FCF of £830m and the 21.4% FCF-yield pass sit on neither printed basis.

It is not a buy on this pack. Adjusted PBT has fallen two years running (£961m restated FY24 → £923m FY25 → £852m FY26). Group LFL turned from +0.3% to −2.1%. Statutory basic EPS is 10.45p → 9.50p → 8.63p. The FY26 chair text itself says adjusted basic EPS of 11.71p (−5.5%) was “supported partly by” the £200m buyback. High Dividend Yield and Financial Health and Economic Moat already failed on the same run that passed Dividend Growth, FCF Yield, Piotroski and Earnings Quality. Size any book as accumulate in sterling filing terms. Do not add on the headline Buy, and do not treat the still-missing August 2026 trading-update RNS as optional colour.

Screen and overlay disagreement. Snapshot buy / conviction_score 1.0 / “Conviction 64%” / failed_models=[] contradicts the same-run manifest (FCF Yield pass on an unreconciled 830 million, High Dividend Yield fail at 0.107, Financial Health fail at 0.80, Economic Moat fail at 0.00) and a research overlay that has already cut to Accumulate / buy. Composite 0.6912 is only a little above the sector 0.599; that does not make 11/22 a clean Buy. This trial does not recycle the snapshot’s repeated Accumulate boilerplate as independent confirmation.

Cyclical sports-fashion / sneaker cycle. cyclical_exposure_detected and cyclical_exposure_overlay are false. The name is catalogued Consumer Cyclical. FY26 LFL was −2.1% in a promotional market with declining store footfall. News on 19–20 August 2026 frames a second profit warning in three months, a ~£50m FY27 cut, US and footwear softness, and an 11–14% share drop — titles only, no statutory Q2. Nike read-across on 1 July 2026 and RBC “promotional / lack of brand heat” on 3 August 2026 are the same cycle, not a separate story. P/E 9.0 / P/B 1.3 may already price a trough; they do not prove the trough is only cyclical rather than a structural North America / footwear / brand-heat problem. Economic Moat scored 0.00 on the same run.

PRIMARY-FILING GAP and interim quality. interim_quality_overlay is false. Catalog interim_count=0 and trading_update_count=0. The live operating print is headline news, ranked below empty Yahoo quarterlies. Do not invent August trading-update statutory figures from WSJ / This is Money / Yahoo titles. The first warning referenced as “three months prior” has no date or magnitude in the manifest. Trade must wait on an ingested August TU or the next H1 statutory body before any upgrade from accumulate.

FCF definition and the 21.4% yield. Company £462m versus Yahoo £956m versus screen £830m is an unresolved definition split, and fcf_definition_divergence is wrongly false. The cash dividend is covered on the company basis. The FY26 buyback is also covered on that basis. Combined FY26 cash returns of about £253m leave headroom against £462m and against ex-lease net cash of about £311m — more comfortable than a ~£31m OCR misread, and still thin once a second £200m programme, a news-only earnings cut, and a £1.5bn Genesis window are restored. Do not pass FCF Yield at 21.4% without stating the basis.

Leverage after leases, Hibbett debt and Genesis. Screen cheapness does not restore IFRS 16 (Yahoo leases 3,138 million), financial debt of about 542 million, or the £1.5bn NCI cap. Printed net leverage 1.4x is a lease-inclusive ratio next to Yahoo normalised EBITDA of 1,938 million, not an unlevered cash box. The FY25 Hibbett $700m term loan and planned H1 FY26 refinancing are not closed in the FY26 extract. cash_conversion_overlay is false despite OCF “over £1.3bn” compressing to company FCF of £462m.

Share-count shrinkage versus EPS / ROE quality. Weighted-average diluted shares 5,160 million to 5,112 million do little of the work; year-end ordinary shares 5,183 million to 4,921 million do more for the per-share dividend and for screen ROE 13.7%. The filing already admits the buyback supported adjusted EPS. How much of the quality/GARP stack is shrinkage rather than operations is only partly resolved, and the unread TVR is required for the FY27 programme.

Governance and key person. Andrew Higginson stepped down at the 21 July 2026 AGM. News: Darren Shapland interim chair; Peter Agnefjäll appointed from 1 September 2026. CEO pressure appears only in pre-update headlines. Pentland control is not in the assigned extracts.

Accounting and unit hygiene. FY26 statements, Note 4 and the APM section are missing from the assigned extract. Yahoo unusual items −150 million and impairments 119 million are not a substitute. Summary limits of £80.66 / £77.41 (manifest still has £85.58 / £80.08, ATR 3.57) match LSE pence, not pounds. trade_plan is null. Those strings are not research targets and are not used to size a book here. Conviction 1.0 versus “Conviction 64%” versus manifest 0.4003 is a schema defect.

Watch. Ingest of the 20 August 2026 trading update and the next H1 statutory body; remaining FY27 £200m buyback versus TVR; FY27 guidance checkpoints; Nike / footwear read-across; Genesis £1.5bn window; chair/CEO; company FCF versus £462m / £956m / £830m; ex-lease net cash versus the ~£311m print; alert if filings_index fetch time post-dates a results or guidance headline that has no body, or if snapshot adjusted_signal stays buy while research_verdict stays accumulate.
